agent_vs_you: The agent picked 'video-edit' (Magic Hour's generative ai-video-editor). It was not wired, so the harness wrote a placeholder SVG and reported the step 'done'. Even if wired, it was the wrong tool: a generative editor re-renders footage, and the must-haves demand only source footage with no speed change and the original audio in sync. A cut is a code job, 'trim' (exact range, nothing regenerated), and the catalogue had it. But trim needs a 'from' and 'to', and choosing the 8 interesting seconds needs to SEE the clip. The planner only gets the filename, and no catalogue tool turns a clip into a shot list with timestamps, so the agent had nothing to choose a range from. It probably reached for video-edit because it is the only tool that sounds like it decides what to cut. Looking at the clip: 0–3 s jets cruising, 3–11 s cockpit lines ('Hook, you with me?' / 'Right here, Vega.'), 11.4–16.6 s a static ship with a caption card and a targeting display, 16.6–25.7 s missile launch, hits and the ship exploding, 25.7–29 s jets leaving, then an end card. The best 8 s is the continuous action from the 16.57 s scene cut to 24.57 s.

your_plan.say: I'll keep the action: an 8-second stretch from the missile launch to the ship exploding, cut straight from your clip with its original sound, nothing regenerated.
